proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses the observed-margin, consistency, latent-ignorability, treatment-odds, and outcome-odds restrictions to construct interior compatible laws, as well as the exposure-region, mixture-root, adjusted-mean, and binary-mixture-inversion nodes.  Adding these direct edges makes the declared proof spine complete; the claim is unchanged.

proposed.statement: Let all three budgets diverge and allow a sequence of compatible laws with \(w_{1,x}\to1\), \(w_{0,x}\to0\), \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=1,X=x)\to1\), and \(\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=0,X=x)\to0\).  Then \([L,R]\) converges to the binary-outcome Manski interval \(\left[\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}-p_x\},\;\sum_x\lambda_x\{p_xr_{1,x}-(1-p_x)r_{0,x}+1-p_x\}\right]\).  No Manski-recovery claim is made at finite budgets or under latent positivity bounded away from zero.
proposed.justification: The all-budget limit locates the model between point identification and unrestricted treatment-response bounds without overstating finite-budget coverage.
proposed.gap: Imbens relates unrestricted sensitivity to worst-case bounds qualitatively; this proposition gives the exact common-binary-\(U\) endpoint limit and the required loss of latent positivity.
proposed.consumer: Users can interpret very large budgets against a familiar worst-case benchmark and detect implementations that converge to the wrong limit.
